cells.tense: You're sitting with someone and you can feel where they are without leaving where you are.
cells.ask: Say one true thing to someone today and let it stand. Notice what you kept back for yourself.
cells.core:
You feel where someone is and you stay yourself while it happens. Their mood reaches you and doesn't take the wheel. You're open without dissolving into them, and that combination is rarer than either half on its own.

Something you used to grip has been set down, maybe without ceremony, and it isn't taking up your hands anymore. The pull now is to make the connection wider — say more, do more, be more present — and you don't have to obey it. Sit where you are and put down one more thing. The sitting is yours to keep, and what you release becomes room someone else can move in.
cells.sheetLine: You feel them fully and you're still here.
cells.verb: feeling with someone rather than only about them
cells.place: where you set down what you no longer need to carry

cells.tense: You're already rehearsing tomorrow's difficulty tonight, so you'll be ready to hold it when it lands.
cells.ask: Name one thing you're braced to carry for someone and hand it back for an hour. Tell them you've done it.
cells.core:
You keep reaching past the present moment. Before anyone has asked, you're testing how their trouble would sit on you, what might go wrong, what you'll need to absorb — and that rehearsal has stopped being care. You walk into rooms already bearing something nobody gave you.

Closeness is bending here. You live inside other people's feelings and out of touch with your own, and a load you could set down stays held because setting it down reads as abandoning them. Pick one thing that isn't yours to carry. Not permanently. An hour. Whatever stays underneath — that's what they were trying to reach.
cells.sheetLine: You're bracing to hold what hasn't arrived.
cells.verb: feeling with someone rather than only about them
cells.place: where you set down what you no longer need to carry

cells.tense: You stopped reaching toward people a while back, and you're still standing at a door that's already shut.
cells.ask: Send one message that tells someone one plain fact about your day. Nothing more is asked of them than reading it.
cells.core:
The good version of this is small and you'd recognize it if it happened: you're with someone, their mood touches you, and you stay in the room while it does. Connected without becoming one thing — you say what you think, they can disagree, and neither of you flinches. That's what's absent right now.

The distance you keep is steady and it costs you nothing visible. In rooms with people, they stay a certain size — not cold, just not entered. Your day goes on being your own private thing. One sentence saying something true about how today went would be enough. You don't have to hand anyone the whole day, and the door doesn't have to swing wide. A gap will do.
cells.sheetLine: You keep them at a size that doesn't cost.

cells.tense: People keep saying they feel close to you, and you keep answering as if they said something else.
cells.ask: Catch one moment today when someone turns toward you. Don't smooth it away. Say out loud that you're glad they did.
cells.core:
You'd tell it plain: closeness isn't your department. You keep things practical and slightly to the side. And people lean in anyway — they tell you things they keep from other people. Warmth moves through the room and you're part of how it gets there, while your own sense of it stays switched off.

The setting down, for you, is the story where you're not in it. Not becoming expressive. Just not stepping around what arrives. You don't have to feel it first — notice it second and say so. When you stop moving out of its way, the recognition has somewhere to land.
cells.sheetLine: They turn to you. You keep calling it nothing.

Someone might object that they're simply private, not shut — and the ask still works, because it's a one-person, one-minute act that gives them an exit. The sentence that serves me is the neat turn 'and what they meet is you' — it sounds like a close and the person may hear a verdict instead of an offer, so I keep the ask and skip the summary.
